items.author: main session (sprint 58 military design, 2026-10-26)
items.title: Seven land classes by equipment generation, and their equipment as goods
items.design: MILITARY.md § Land — the classes. Infantry, motorised, mechanised, armour, light armour, artillery, air defence; each a class x equipment generation with soft, hard, hardness, defence, breakthrough. Equipment goods (small arms, armoured vehicles and artillery pieces by generation, air defence systems, drones) with recipes; hire buys the class's kit off the shelf. FPV drones are equipment raising soft/hard attack. Tech gates generations (DIGITISATION_TREE ST-FO). The campaign roster table is the class table; the Era -1 nineteen rows are untouched.

items.author: main session (sprint 58 military design, 2026-10-26)
items.title: Wounded units refit from the shelf; spent units retreat; readiness recovers out of contact
items.design: MILITARY.md § Land — equipment, refit and manpower. Each tick a unit below full HP draws equipment and manpower to regain HP; unmet draws leave it wounded. A unit at readiness 0 moves one tile away from the enemy (a legal march, deterministic tile pick). Readiness recovers out of contact, capped by morale. Morale is per unit, moved by supply, victories, losses and war exhaustion. Conservation: men and goods drawn equal HP regained.

items.author: main session (sprint 58 military design, 2026-10-26)
items.title: A bunker building adds defence and hardness to the units on its tile
items.design: MILITARY.md § Fortifications. A building type; units on its tile gain defence, defenders gain hardness. Degraded by artillery and strikes, repaired over time. Rivals build bunkers too: granted (Ben, 2026-10-31), AI_OPPONENT.md § 11 "Rival nations build bunkers on their own ground" - own ground only, scored over its fronts, units and the build price, through the player's build verb.

items.author: main session (sprint 58 military design, 2026-10-26)

items.design: MILITARY.md § Missiles and § Space. items.author: main session (cold review of BL-1434/BL-1446)
items.title: Hire and refit check goods by price as well as quantity; the PNG inflate gets an output cap
items.design: Cold review of unit designs, 2026-10-28. (1) HIGH, latent until later kit unlocks (BL-1436): hire_goods_affordable counts shelf quantity only, while buy_from_corp_shelves charges the posted price capped by purse_room_of, and debit_kit_goods ignores how much it bought. A design refit (0 credits) with a committed treasury gets its kit free; a hire at exact room drops the treasury below its commitments. The row-goods leg had the flaw already. Fix: the affordability check sums qty x posted price plus the credit cost against purse_room_of, and apply asserts the bought amount. (2) LOW: hire_goods_affordable prices each row axis at its first candidate without the kit draw on the same resource, so an affordable hire can be refused. (3) LOW: png_decode.cpp inflate has no output cap; stop once out exceeds h x (stride+1). (4) LOW: the refit menu labels a design refit with the row gate (+ kit) and omits the changed slots goods; an obsolete own row moves the (live design) entry to the end.

items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-10-30)
items.title: Recruits: bases make land and air recruits from their province's people; hires and refills spend them
items.design: Written in MILITARY.md § Recruits (Ben, 2026-10-30). A military base makes land recruits and an airbase air recruits, a fixed number per quarter (economy.military.recruits), each taken from the population centres of the base's province, largest first. One national land pool and one air pool, capped at 15x the theatre's quarterly output. A hire spends its men (a wing its crew) and is refused when the pool cannot fill it; a unit below full men refills from the pool at a Logistic Point cost per recruit paid at its paying road, as supply is. Bases carry no upkeep. The Recruit tab heads each theatre with its pool. Supersedes BL-1424 (soldiers from labour). Save bump (the two pools). Measure the population drain and G1t50 before tuning the rate; rivals hire through the same gate.
